items.section: ティー・ソフトドリンク / Tea & Soft Drinks
items.note: Hot or iced. Made with real cocoa and steamed milk rather than a sachet — the reliable order for a child.

items.section: ティー・ソフトドリンク / Tea & Soft Drinks
items.note: Apple, mango and guava-and-grape are also ¥420.

items.section: ティー・ソフトドリンク / Tea & Soft Drinks
items.note: A South African bottled sparkling drink made from 100% pressed apple juice, no added sugar. It has a small cult following in Japanese cafés as the grown-up soft drink.
You can drink it on the bench outside, looking into the woods of Hinoyama.

toba_ephemere.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. These six are the full grand menu, transcribed from a Mie food blog that photographed the board; the college's own announcement and a Chunichi Shimbun news piece independently confirm 'six varieties, ¥500-700 tax included', which matches exactly — hence high confidence despite no shop-published price list being reachable (the shop's menu lives in an Instagram Story highlight, グランドメニュー, which cannot be fetched). The shop also runs short-run seasonal crepes — e.g. a three-portion ゴリのチョコバナナ and a とろけるバニラのショコラベリーフレンチ, both ¥1,500, in March 2026 — so check the counter for the current limited item. Context worth knowing: 'Ephemere' is French for 'fleeting/short-lived', and the shop means it — it is run by three students from Toba National College of Maritime Technology's advanced course as a fixed-term venture that closes in February 2027. Takeaway only, cash or PayPay, on the 2nd floor of Toba Ichibangai right in front of Toba Station; eating while walking is banned inside the building, so there is a seating space beside the shop. Open Mon and Fri-Sun 13:00 to the mall's closing time, closed Tue-Thu.

items.en: The plain one — a hot crepe with butter and dusted sugar, nothing else
items.note: The classic 'sucre' crepe and the best way to judge the batter. Cheapest item on the board.

items.en: Savoury crepe with ham, melted cheese and cracked black pepper
items.note: The only savoury item — a nod to the Breton galette that crepes come from, which is traditionally the savoury half of the pair.

items.en: Crepe wrapped around grilled mochi rice cake, nori seaweed and a piece of rice cracker — sweet-savoury and very chewy
items.note: The most local thing on the menu: the nori is harvested off Toshi-jima, the fishing island out in Toba Bay. Isobe-maki (mochi wrapped in nori) is a standard Japanese snack; this puts it in a crepe.

items.en: Chocolate sauce, banana and whipped cream
items.note: Listed by the shop as the number-one seller with children — the default Japanese crepe-stand order.

items.en: Crepe filled with apple and topped with shards of crisp pastry, so it eats like an apple pie
items.note: The pastry topping is added at the counter so it stays crunchy.

items.en: Ise green tea kneaded into the crepe batter, filled with sweet azuki bean paste, shiratama rice dumplings and matcha chocolate
items.note: The shop's signature and the priciest item. 'Kintoki' on a Japanese dessert menu means sweetened azuki beans. Mie is a major tea prefecture, so the Ise-cha in the batter is a local ingredient, and it makes the crepe noticeably chewier and less sweet than the others.

items.ja: 御客前バイキング しんわダイニング「天・地・海」
items.en: Cook-in-front-of-you seafood buffet, the inn's main dinner format
items.note: A 10 m open kitchen where chefs fry, grill and finish dishes as you watch, plus a nightly whole-fish butchering show (解体ショー), a wood-fired pizza oven, sashimi and sushi, rice cooked in an earthen kamado, a salad bar and free soft drinks. Served 18:00–21:00 to staying and day-trip guests. Buffet labels carry coloured allergen stickers for egg, crustacean, wheat, dairy and sesame/nuts — but only for main ingredients, not for seasonings or dashi.

items.ja: 御客前会席 回転展望レストラン「東風と海」
items.en: Multi-course kaiseki dinner in the slowly revolving panoramic restaurant
items.note: The alternative to the buffet: a set kaiseki menu finished in front of you, course by course, in a restaurant that rotates over Toba Bay. Last entry 19:00. Allergy requests go through the inn's enquiry form in advance.

items.en: Whole live Ise spiny lobster served as sashimi in its own shell
items.note: The Ise-Shima signature. The lobster is presented whole, the tail meat sliced raw and sweet; the head is usually taken away and returned as soup or grilled. Ordered on top of your dinner plan. Domestic lobster.

items.en: Whole Ise spiny lobster sashimi paired with live abalone sashimi
items.note: The blow-out version: Mie's two most prized shellfish on one platter. Abalone is served still twitching on the shell — chewy, faintly sweet, eaten with soy and wasabi or a squeeze of citrus.

items.en: Half an Ise spiny lobster grilled in the shell
items.note: 'Keshoyaki' means grilling it with the bright red shell left on as its own garnish. Simple, smoky, and the cheapest step onto the lobster ladder here. Domestic lobster.

items.en: Ise spiny lobster simmered whole in sweet soy broth
items.note: 'Gusoku' means a samurai's suit of armour — the lobster's shell. A local home-style treatment: the whole lobster braised in soy, sake and sugar until the meat takes on the dark broth. Soy-based, so wheat is likely.
Live abalone sliced raw on the shell. Toba's ama divers have harvested abalone here for centuries and it is still offered at Ise Jingu. Firm, almost crunchy, with a clean sea-sweetness.

items.en: Small abalone pan-grilled as a steak
items.note: 'Hime' (princess) abalone is the small grade. Cooked on a hot plate with butter and usually a soy-butter sauce, which turns it tender rather than chewy — an easier introduction than raw abalone.

items.ja: 松阪牛石板焼 A4等級 1人前（約80g）
items.en: A4-grade Matsusaka beef grilled on a hot stone at your table
items.note: Matsusaka is Mie's own wagyu brand and among the most marbled beef in Japan. You sear the slices yourself on the heated stone; dipping sauces are normally soy-based.

Ise-Shima's fisherman's dish: bonito (katsuo) sliced and marinated in sweet soy, then spread over vinegared rice with shiso, ginger and nori. The name comes from crews mixing the catch into the rice by hand (te-kone) on the boat. Sold here only as a big tray for a group.

items.en: Assorted shellfish grilled in the shell (winter only)
items.note: Seasonal October–February. Typically turban shell, clams and scallop grilled over heat and finished with a splash of soy — the classic Toba seaside plate.

February only. Toba's Momotori and Uramura oysters are famous nationally; here they are baked with a Western topping rather than eaten raw. Gratin toppings normally mean breadcrumbs and/or a flour roux, so not gluten-free.

items.en: Savoury steamed egg custard, winter season
items.note: Silky, barely-set egg custard steamed with dashi and small treasures buried inside — usually chicken, prawn, gingko nut and mushroom. Eaten hot, with a spoon.

items.en: Rolled omelette made with dashi stock
items.note: Layer upon layer of thin egg rolled around itself, loose and juicy from the bonito dashi mixed into the batter. A benchmark dish for any Japanese kitchen.

items.en: Children's plate: fried prawn, karaage, mini hamburg, chips, three-kind sashimi, omurice, salad and soup
items.note: The full Japanese kids' set. Contains breaded fried prawn and flour-coated fried chicken.

items.en: Toddler plate: mini hamburg, gratin cocotte, penne in mayonnaise, chips, mini omelette, chicken rice, salad, soup, dessert
items.note: For smaller children. Gratin and penne mean wheat and dairy.

items.en: Baby food: soft rice porridge with kombu dashi, Hokkaido corn, diced vegetables and chopped fruit
items.note: The 7-month version uses Mie-grown white rice cooked to a soft porridge with kombu dashi and de-salted baby whitebait; the 5-month version (¥550) is plain rice porridge, corn, seasonal fruit and a toddler drink.

items.en: Ketchup-fried rice wrapped in a thin omelette
items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Japan's comfort-food classic — chicken and rice fried with ketchup, sealed in egg. A safe order for a child, or for anyone tired of seafood.

items.en: Japanese-style minced beef-and-pork patty, no bun
items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Served as a plated steak with sauce, not in a bun. Japanese hamburg is bound with panko breadcrumbs, so it contains wheat.

items.en: Head-on prawn in panko breadcrumbs, deep-fried
items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Head left on for looks and for the crisp roasted head meat. Panko coating — wheat.

items.en: Japanese fried chicken, marinated then dusted and fried
items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Marinated in soy, sake and ginger, dusted with starch or flour and fried twice for crunch.

items.en: Three-kind sashimi plate sized for children
items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Mild, familiar cuts in small portions. The soy sauce on the side contains wheat unless you ask for tamari.

items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: The a la carte version of the winter chawanmushi, orderable year-round from the single-dish list.

items.en: Plain wheat udon noodles in broth, no toppings
items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: The cheapest thing on the list and a reliable plain late meal. Wheat noodles; the broth is bonito dashi, so not vegan.

items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Potato only, but fried in oil shared with breaded items.

items.section: アラカルト単品 / A la carte
items.note: Usually made with milk or cream and a flour thickener — worth confirming.

toba_todaya_coffee_shop.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. No price list is published anywhere for this tearoom; the four items below are the categories Todaya's own site and guest photos actually confirm.

items.note: The tearoom corner on Todaya's ground floor, looking straight out over Toba Bay — it is a rest stop inside the inn rather than a full café. The inn's own site describes the offering simply as coffee and tea plus some local Mie drinks.
Served alongside the coffee; milk on request.
Todaya's site advertises 'local drinks' without naming them; in Mie that usually means Ise green tea, mikan juice or a regional soda. Ask what is on that day.
Photographed by guests as a complimentary serving rather than a priced item. Thick, very sweet red-bean soup with a piece of grilled rice cake sunk in it — the standard Japanese inn welcome sweet.

toba_oshokujidokoro_tomae.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Todaya's own site names the menu but publishes no prices for it.

items.note: Tomae is Todaya's oyashoku-dokoro — the late-night snack room, open from 18:00, aimed at guests coming out of the karaoke lounges. The inn's site names its house ramen as the headline: as it puts it, the proper end to a night out is ramen. Wheat noodles in a soy-seasoned broth.
Hand-formed salted rice, usually wrapped in nori with a filling such as pickled plum, salmon or simmered kombu. The filling decides the flags — ask.

items.en: Thick wheat noodles in hot broth
items.note: The other late-night staple. Bonito dashi broth, so not vegan.

toba_toba_kokusai_hotel_washo.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. This is a set-course restaurant: there is no a la carte list. Course contents are the Apr–Sep 2026 menu and rotate seasonally. A private room is ¥11,000 extra (up to 14 guests).

items.ja: リゾートWashoku 坂手 〜伊勢海老付〜
items.en: Entry kaiseki course built around Ise spiny lobster
items.note: Named after one of the islands in Toba Bay. Current run: welcome dish; first tray of sake snacks, sea bream in clear broth and assorted sashimi; the headline aroma-steamed Ise lobster with two sauces; second tray of the day's fish cooked to your choice plus soft-simmered octopus with vegetables; clay-pot rice, soup and pickles; sweet of the day. Lunch service only for parties of 8+ booked 3 days ahead.

items.ja: リゾートWashoku 菅島 〜伊勢海老・鮑付〜
items.en: Mid kaiseki course with both Ise lobster and abalone
items.note: Adds abalone grilled with a dairy-miso glaze and steamed with seaweed, kuruma prawn in the sashimi tray, and Ise lobster simmered Yoshino-style (in a light kudzu-thickened broth) on the second tray. Lunch for parties of 6+ on 3 days' notice.

items.ja: リゾートWashoku 答志 〜伊勢海老・鮑・松阪牛付〜
items.en: Top kaiseki course: Ise lobster, abalone and Matsusaka beef
items.note: Mie's 'three great flavours' in one sitting. Includes abalone roasted on hot stone, Ise lobster grilled in soy-butter, a small sukiyaki pot of Matsusaka beef, sea-bream tekone-zushi, and onigara-jiru — the intense soup made from the pounded lobster shell.

items.ja: 料理長おまかせ 神島 〜三重の三大味覚「伊勢海老・鮑・松阪牛付」〜
items.en: Chef's omakase menu, the restaurant's flagship
items.note: Composed on the day from whatever came in: clear soup, seasonal sake snacks, sashimi, a dish finished in front of you, the day's best fish cooked however you choose, Matsusaka beef fillet, nigiri sushi, soup, rice and pickles, sweet of the day. Book 3 days ahead.

Genuinely rare in this region, and stated by the hotel to use no animal ingredients at all — vegetables, mushrooms, grains and fruit only. Runs: taro dumpling; appetiser of seasonal tofu, kinpira vegetables, assorted vegetable sushi and a steamed dish; steamed-vegetable clear soup; sashimi-style konnyaku; stone-roasted vegetables as the main; vegetable tempura, simmered vegetables and miso-glazed grilled aubergine; clay-pot rice with nori, pounded plum and simmered shiitake; pickles; fruit. Tempura batter means wheat, so say so if you also need gluten-free. Order by 16:00 two days ahead.

items.ja: お子様メニュー かもめ
items.note: A lacquer box with simmered beef, grilled fish, rolled egg, simmered prawn and sashimi, plus fish-and-vegetable tempura, rice, red miso soup and ice cream. Tempura = wheat.

items.ja: お子様メニュー みつしま
items.en: Children's set, middle size — includes Ise lobster
items.note: Deep-fried sea bass to start, assorted sashimi, silky chawanmushi, Western-style grilled Ise lobster, tempura, simmered beef, rice, red miso soup, pickles and dessert.

items.ja: お子様メニュー やまとたちばな
items.note: Named after the rare native citrus that is Toba city's tree. Effectively a scaled-down adult kaiseki.

items.en: Sake tasting flight, three 60 ml glasses
items.note: Three seasonally chosen Mie local sakes poured chilled in tasting glasses — the easiest way to find what you like without committing to a bottle. Dinner service only.

toba_nagatokan.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Ise lobster and abalone are sold at market price (時価) and the shellfish prices move with the beach price. There is also a sashimi-by-the-plate list (tuna ¥930〜, sea bream ¥730〜, turban shell ¥730〜, sweet shrimp / squid / scallop / chopped octopus ¥630〜, vinegared dish ¥520〜) and drinks from ¥350 (soft drinks) / ¥480 (sake, 1 gō) / ¥580 (beer, highball, shōchū, chūhai).

items.en: Tekone-zushi set: soy-marinated bonito over vinegared rice, with Ise udon
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: Limited to 30 a day. Ise-Shima's fisherman's dish — bonito sliced and steeped in sweet soy, then laid over sushi rice with nori and shiso; the name comes from crews mixing it by hand (te-kone) on the boat. The set pairs it with Ise udon, the region's other icon: fat, extremely soft wheat noodles with no soup at all, just a puddle of near-black sweet tamari tare you stir through. Plus a small side, miso soup and pickles.

items.en: Signature seafood rice bowl — assorted raw fish over rice
items.note: The house favourite: whatever came off the Toba boats that morning, sliced and fanned over rice. Served with mekabu (the frilly root end of wakame, sticky and mineral-tasting), pickles and miso soup. The restaurant's other menu page prints a fuller version at ¥2,300 with extra side dishes.

items.en: Sashimi set meal, five kinds of fish
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: Five cuts of local fish with a vinegared side, a small dish, miso soup, rice and pickles — the standard way to eat sashimi as a full meal rather than as a starter.

items.en: Sashimi set meal, seven kinds of fish
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: The bigger platter; the shop also prints a six-kind version at ¥2,600. Ask what is best that day — Toba's line-up changes with the season.

items.en: Shellfish set: grilled shellfish plus raw shellfish sashimi
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: Toba is shellfish country, and this set gives you both treatments — some grilled in the shell, some sliced raw — with a vinegared side, small dish, rice, miso soup and pickles.

items.en: Two large panko-fried prawns as a set meal
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: Three-prawn version ¥2,440; a jumbo two-prawn version is ¥2,760. Comes with a vinegared dish, small side, miso soup, rice and pickles. Panko coating — wheat.

items.en: Ise spiny lobster, breaded and deep-fried, as a set meal
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: The local lobster given the Japanese fry-shop treatment — split, crumbed and fried, served with tartare. Indulgent, and far cheaper than eating the same lobster raw. With small side, pickles, miso soup and rice.

items.en: Mixed deep-fried set — prawn and assorted fry
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: The safe all-rounder if raw fish is not your thing. Panko-crumbed, wheat throughout.

items.en: Breaded pork loin cutlet served sizzling on an iron plate
items.section: 郷土の御膳 / Local set meals
items.note: With salad, aka-dashi (the darker red-miso soup of the Tokai region), a small dish, pickles and white rice — and the house's own miso dare sauce, which the shop specifically tells you to try. Nagoya-style miso-katsu in spirit.

items.ja: 帆立バター焼き＆海老フライ定食
items.en: Butter-grilled scallops with fried prawn, as a set
items.note: Combines the two crowd-pleasers, with mekabu seaweed, a small dish, rice and miso soup.

items.en: Scallops grilled in butter, in the shell
items.note: The chef's own pick, per the shop. Scallops in their fan shells with butter melting over them on a small brazier — sweet and rich, usually finished with a dash of soy.
Crisp shell, soft sweet scallop inside. Panko — wheat.

items.en: Abalone grilled in butter on the shell
items.note: Abalone is a designated Mie 'brand' ingredient, dived for by Toba's ama. Butter-grilling softens it, and this is the house's most popular abalone dish — easier eating than raw abalone, which is famously chewy.

items.en: Whole Ise spiny lobster simmered in sweet soy broth
items.note: 'Gusoku' means a warrior's suit of armour — a nod to the lobster's shell. One of the traditional Ise-Shima ways of cooking it, and a local comfort dish rather than a showpiece. Soy-based broth, so wheat is likely.

items.en: Tiny dried whitebait simmered sweet-savoury in soy and ginger
items.note: Cooked fresh in-house. Shigure-ni is a Mie speciality technique — simmering down in soy, mirin and ginger until sticky. Eaten in small pinches over rice; also travels well as a souvenir.

items.en: Chilled buckwheat noodles on a bamboo tray with dipping sauce
items.note: With mekabu seaweed ¥930. You dip the cold noodles into a small cup of soy-dashi tsuyu. Japanese soba is nearly always cut with wheat flour, and the tsuyu is soy plus bonito.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き 伊勢海老
items.en: Ise spiny lobster to grill yourself on the tabletop net
items.note: 'Teppari' is the local Toba word for 'a huge amount of food', and it is this restaurant's signature format: raw seafood brought to the table and grilled over a net in front of you. Small and large lobster are both sold at the day's market price.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き あわび
items.en: Live abalone to grill at the table
items.note: It moves on the grill as it cooks — startling the first time. Cook until the edges curl, then cut and dip.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き 車海老
items.en: Japanese tiger prawns for the tabletop grill
items.note: Grilled in the shell with a pinch of salt; the head is worth eating once it crisps.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き サザエ（2個）
items.en: Two turban shells grilled whole in the shell
items.note: Sazae is the spiky sea snail sold all along Toba's 'Sazae Street'. Grilled in its own juices with a splash of soy; you spiral the meat out with a pick. The dark coil at the tail end is the liver — bitter, and locals eat it.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き 大アサリ（1個）
items.en: One giant clam, grilled open in the shell
items.note: A Tokai-coast speciality — far bigger and meatier than an ordinary asari clam, grilled until it pops open and dressed with soy. Two or three bites.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き 白はまぐり（1〜3個）
items.en: White hard clams grilled in the shell
items.note: Hamaguri are the prized big clams of Mie's Ise Bay; the sweet liquor inside is the point, so do not tip it out when the shell opens.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き あっぱっぱ貝
items.en: Local 'appappa' shellfish, grilled in the shell
items.note: A small local bivalve known by its Toba dialect name — cheap, sweet, and about the most 'this is a fishing port' thing on the grill.

items.ja: てっぱり網焼き 緋扇貝
items.en: Noble scallop, grilled in its brightly coloured shell
items.note: The shells come in orange, purple, yellow and red and people take them home. Sweet like a small scallop, and the cheapest thing on the grill list.

items.en: Set shellfish grill course for the table
items.note: White hamaguri clam, scallop, sazae turban shell, appappa shellfish, squid and grilled vegetables, plus rice, miso soup and a small dish — the easy way to order the teppari grill without picking item by item. The shop will also build a course to your budget.

toba_shokujidokoro_taiheiyo_j.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. This shop posts no fixed printed menu online; almost everything is sold by the piece from the live tanks at the counter, and shellfish/lobster prices move with size and season. Figures below are what diners actually paid between 2021 and 2026.

items.en: Mixed grill of four shellfish — one hiougi scallop, one clam, one oyster and one turban shell, cooked over charcoal in front of you
items.note: The house's easiest order and the classic sazae-street experience: the owner lifts the shellfish out of the tank at the door, grills them on the counter hibachi and hands them over in the shell. Contents change with the day's catch.

items.en: Giant summer rock oyster, served raw on the half shell with lemon (grilled on request)
items.note: Different animal from the winter Urimura oyster: iwagaki are in season roughly June-August, grow to a fist's size and are so big the staff will cut one into pieces for you. A larger grade runs about ¥1,500; the price was ¥880 back in 2021, so expect it to keep drifting.

items.en: Charcoal-grilled oysters, sold by the piece (about three to an order)
items.note: Toba's Urimura bay just over the hill is one of Japan's best-known oyster farms, so the winter oysters here are extremely local. Price quoted is for three.

items.en: Turban shell grilled whole in its own shell with a splash of soy, eaten by winkling the meat out with a skewer
items.note: The dish the street is named after — Toba station's row of shops is literally called Sazae Street. You get a metal pick and dig the spiral of meat out yourself; the dark tail end is the liver, bitter and prized. Staff will help if you struggle.

items.en: Raw turban shell, sliced thin — crunchy, faintly sweet, with the liver served alongside
items.note: Anything in the tank can be ordered either raw (お造り) or grilled (浜焼き) — that choice is the whole ordering system here.

items.en: Live abalone sliced raw, firm and mildly sweet, usually with its liver on the side
items.note: Toba's ama (women free-divers) have harvested abalone here for centuries; it is the single most prestigious thing in the tank after the lobster. Priced by the individual shell — ask before ordering.

items.en: Abalone grilled in butter until the edges curl — richer and more tender than the raw version
items.note: The usual choice for people who find raw abalone too chewy. Contains dairy.

items.en: Ise spiny lobster, picked live from the tank and served either as sashimi or split and grilled
items.section: 伊勢海老 / Ise spiny lobster
items.note: Ise-ebi is the emblem of this coast — a clawless spiny lobster, sweeter and stickier on the tongue than a Maine lobster. You choose your own animal and the price follows its size: roughly ¥6,000 for a mid-size one, about ¥9,000 for the biggest. Diners report it still moving when it reaches the counter.

items.ja: 伊勢海老の頭（味噌汁／焼き）
items.en: The lobster's head, brought back afterwards either grilled or simmered into miso soup — your choice
items.section: 伊勢海老 / Ise spiny lobster
items.note: Standard practice once you order a whole lobster, and the best part of it: the head holds the dense orange 'miso' (tomalley). Miso soup is wheat-containing unless you check.

items.en: 'Big clam' — a palm-sized surf clam grilled in the shell and brushed with soy
items.note: A Mie/Aichi coastal standard, sold at every festival stall along Ise Bay. Meaty and slightly chewy, closer to a scallop than to a little asari clam despite the name.

items.en: Grilled hard clam — plump, mild and full of its own broth
items.note: Drink the liquor left in the shell before the meat; that is where the flavour is.

items.en: Noble scallop — a small fan scallop with a shell in bright orange, pink or purple, grilled in the shell
items.note: Called appa-gai locally. The candy-coloured shells are farmed around Ise-Shima and are half the fun; the meat is sweeter and softer than a big scallop.

items.en: Whole grilled squid, brushed with soy and cut into rings
items.note: Soy-glazed, so not gluten-free unless you ask for it plain with salt.

items.en: Raw conch (triton shell), sliced thin — very crunchy, clean-tasting
items.note: An unusual thing to see on a menu even in Japan; the same shell blown as a horn by mountain ascetics. Texture is the point.

items.en: Bowl of rice heaped with tiny boiled whitebait, eaten with the shop's sweet soy poured over
items.note: One of the few actual meals here among all the shellfish. Diners note the soy served with it is on the sweet side, which is normal for Mie.

items.en: Tuna sashimi over vinegared or plain rice
items.note: Sliced raw tuna laid over a bowl of rice, usually with shredded nori and wasabi. The plain, filling alternative to a mixed seafood bowl — you pour a little soy over it yourself.

items.en: Spanish mackerel sashimi over rice — the group's signature bowl, made with fish from Toba's Toshi-jima island
items.note: Toshi-jima sawara is a local pride item: lightly seared or raw, oily and soft, quite unlike the grilled sawara sold elsewhere in Japan.

items.en: Ise's own udon — very thick, deliberately soft noodles with no soup, just a small pool of dark, sweet-savoury tare stirred through
items.note: Looks alarmingly dark and tastes far gentler than it looks. It was fast food for Ise Jingu pilgrims, boiled long so it could be served the second a traveller sat down; chewiness is not the goal here. Wheat noodles and a soy/dashi tare.

items.en: Dark red-miso soup, the standard soup of the Nagoya/Mie region
items.note: Made with mame-miso rather than the pale miso used further east; deeper and slightly bitter. Usually contains bonito dashi.

items.en: Plain white rice, orderable on its own
items.note: Worth knowing about: several shops on this street only sell rice as part of a donburi, and reviewers single this place out for letting you order a plain bowl to go with the grilled shellfish.

items.en: Draft beer, highballs, whisky and local Mie sake
items.note: Around ¥550 a glass. Beer and whisky are not gluten-free; sake is made from rice.

toba_gohanya_fukutsugi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Daily-special prices come from the shop's own Instagram posts (2025-2026) and have crept from ¥900 to ¥990 over that period; standing-menu prices are from diners' menu-board photos.

items.en: Daily set meal — one main dish plus rice, miso soup and two or three small vegetable side dishes
items.note: The thing to order. The husband-and-wife owners post that day's main on Instagram (@hukutsugi) each morning, and chalk it on a board by the door. Sides rotate: shredded daikon simmered in dashi, bean-sprout namul, a mayo salad, pickled daikon. Price was ¥900-¥980 through 2024-25 and is ¥990 as of Aug 2026.

items.en: Fried chicken in a sweet soy glaze, as a set meal
items.note: One of the most frequent daily specials. Flour-coated and soy-glazed.
A chicken breast or thigh flattened, crumbed in panko and deep-fried, served with shredded cabbage, rice, miso soup and small sides. Eaten with thick brown tonkatsu sauce poured over it.

items.en: Chilled thin-sliced pork, blanched and served cold over vegetables with a dipping sauce
items.note: A summer rotation — one of the few non-fried mains here. Sauce is usually sesame or ponzu, both of which normally contain soy sauce.

items.en: Mixed deep-fried set — an assortment of breaded items, typically prawn, cheese-stuffed chicken tender and ham cutlet
items.note: Also appears as おまかせフライ (chef's-choice fry). Contents change day to day.

items.en: Chicken tempura — chicken in a light, puffy batter rather than crunchy karaage coating
items.note: A Kyushu dish that has become a regular here; diners describe it as crisp outside, very soft inside. Reported at ¥950 in mid-2025 and ¥980 in 2026.

items.en: Fried chicken under a heavy drizzle of Japanese mayonnaise
items.note: Also runs as 明太マヨ (mayo cut with spicy cod roe) and 唐揚げチリソースマヨ (chilli-sauce mayo, ¥980).

items.en: Chinese-style fried chicken with a tangy soy, vinegar, spring-onion and ginger dressing poured over
items.note: Reported at ¥900 in 2024; the sauce soaks half the coating soft and leaves the rest crisp, which is the whole appeal.

items.en: Fried chicken dipped in sweet vinegar and topped with egg tartar sauce
items.note: Miyazaki's most famous dish, a standard on Japanese diner rotations.

items.en: Pork cutlet dipped in Worcestershire-style sauce and laid straight on rice — no egg
items.note: Different from the more common egg-bound katsudon; the sauce version is drier and sharper.

items.en: Prawns simmered in dashi and bound with softly set egg
items.note: 'Tamago-toji' means bound with egg: the prawns are simmered in sweet soy-dashi with onion, then beaten egg is poured in and left barely set, so it comes out soft and custardy. Served as a full set with rice and miso soup.

items.en: Japanese curry rice with breaded deep-fried prawns on top
items.note: Japanese curry roux is thickened with wheat flour.

items.ja: ふくつぎからあげ定食
items.en: The house fried chicken — salt-seasoned, crackling-crisp outside, juicy inside
items.note: The signature and the thing regulars tell first-timers to order. Salt-based rather than soy-based, so it tastes cleaner than most karaage.

items.ja: にんにくしょう油からあげ定食
items.en: Fried chicken marinated in garlic and soy sauce
items.note: The louder sibling of the house karaage.

items.en: Breaded deep-fried pork loin cutlet set
items.note: The benchmark Japanese cutlet — pork loin, panko-crumbed, deep-fried and cut into strips so you can pick it up with chopsticks. Served with a mountain of shredded raw cabbage, rice and miso soup.

items.en: Pork cutlet under a thick sweet red-miso sauce — the Nagoya/Mie way of eating tonkatsu
items.note: Worth trying here rather than in a chain: the dark mame-miso sauce is a regional signature of this side of Japan.

items.en: Breaded deep-fried pork fillet — leaner and more tender than the loin cutlet
items.note: Also sold as エビ・ヒレカツ定食, paired with a prawn.

items.en: Japanese-style minced-beef-and-pork patty brought out sizzling on a hot iron plate
items.note: Patties are usually bound with breadcrumbs and the sauce is normally soy- or wine-based.

items.ja: エビ・ふくつぎからあげ定食
items.en: Combination set: fried prawns plus the house salt karaage
items.note: Even the standard portion comes with three small side dishes and a mounded bowl of rice.

items.en: Large and 'blast-size' versions of the set meals, listed on their own separate menu sheets
items.note: This is what the shop is locally famous for — bakumori means portions like ten prawns on one plate, and there is a further rice upgrade regulars call manga-mori. Extra rice on a normal set is about +¥170. Order the normal size unless you are certain.

items.en: The daily set packed as a takeaway lunchbox
items.note: Takeaway is taken by phone only (0599-37-7437), and larger orders need advance notice. A steady stream of local phone orders comes in at lunchtime.

toba_tasuke.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. This shop publishes no price list anywhere: the only menus are two handwritten sheets above the counter (今日の鮨メニュー, today's sushi, and 今日の肴メニュー, today's small dishes) that change with the catch, and much of the tank stock is priced by the individual animal. Diners report roughly ¥10,000 per head for a full evening of sashimi, grilled shellfish and nigiri; ¥22,000-¥28,000 for two people eating hard. Beware: the price list circulating online for '太助寿し' (握り寿司 並 ¥1,200 etc.) belongs to an unrelated shop in Tokyo, not to this one.

items.en: Hand-formed nigiri sushi, ordered piece by piece or left to the chef — almost everything except tuna, sea urchin and salmon roe is caught in Ise Bay
items.note: An old-fashioned town sushi bar, open since the late 1970s and run by the founding chef (born 1947) and his wife alone. The rice is the traditional soft, slightly sweet style, and the pieces are made small — regulars say deliberately, so they are easy to eat. Reserve; they cannot take groups of five or more.

items.en: Assorted sashimi of whatever came in that morning — commonly sea bream, striped jack, halfbeak, horse mackerel, bonito, flounder or grouper
items.note: The chef only handles fish in season and refuses to carry anything out of it, so what appears changes completely through the year. Soy sauce for dipping normally contains wheat.

items.en: Ise spiny lobster killed to order and served raw in its shell, meat firm and sweet
items.note: Roughly ¥5,000-¥6,000 depending on size, and only available in season — the shop uses local animals only, so it disappears from the counter in late spring. Autumn is the reliable time.

items.ja: 伊勢海老の味噌汁（あら汁）
items.en: Miso soup made from the lobster's head and shell after you have eaten the meat
items.note: Brought out to finish the meal. You pick red or blended miso. Enormously savoury — the shell does all the work.

items.en: Toba-caught black abalone, sliced raw, with the liver served alongside
items.note: Crunchy and sweeter the longer you chew. The liver here is eaten with a squeeze of lemon; if you dislike it, the chef will simmer it sweet-and-salty instead. Also served as 水貝 (chilled in salted water) and butter-grilled.

items.en: Turban shell grilled whole in its shell — the chef takes it live from the tank in the shop
items.note: Springy meat and a dense, dark liver. Diners single this out as the dish they remember from here. Also served raw as sazae sashimi, liver included.

items.en: Bonito seared hard on the outside, raw within, sliced thick and eaten with plenty of garlic
items.note: Bonito is the fish Ise-Shima is built on. The loin is seared hard over a flame for seconds so the outside chars while the inside stays raw, then chilled, sliced thick and piled with raw garlic, spring onion and ginger, with ponzu poured over. Punchy and completely unlike plain sashimi.

items.en: The dark bloodline meat of the bonito, chopped and dressed with garlic and miso
items.note: A genuinely local, off-menu-feeling item that regulars push on newcomers — the part most restaurants throw away, iron-rich and strong. Also served as ハラモ, the fatty belly strip, which the chef says you cannot get elsewhere.

items.en: House-cured squid pickled in its own salted innards — intense, briny, an drinking snack
items.note: Made in-house. Salty and funky in a way bottled versions are not; a tiny amount goes with a lot of sake.

items.ja: 皮剥（カワハギ）の造り・肝
items.en: Filefish sliced paper-thin with its rich liver, the liver often mashed into the soy to dip the fish in
items.note: Winter is the season and the liver is why people order it — creamy, almost like sea foie gras. Taken live from the tank in front of you.

items.en: Fish heads, collars and bones simmered gently in soy, sake and sugar
items.note: Made from whatever fish was filleted for your sashimi — ask for it once the raw course is done.

items.en: Salt-grilled beltfish — a long silver ribbon fish, delicate and oily
items.note: Beltfish is graded by how many fingers thick it is; a 'five-finger' fish is prized, and regulars call this the best thing on the grill here.

items.en: Grilled oysters from the bay over the hill
items.note: Toba's Urimura oysters are among Japan's best known; winter season.

items.en: Squid tentacles grilled with salt — soft, sweet, and served in an unreasonably generous pile
items.note: Multiple diners comment that one portion is far more than one person expects.

items.en: Savoury steamed egg custard in a cup, with a large prawn set inside
items.note: Silky rather than rubbery here; the dashi is what people praise. Contains bonito dashi and usually a little soy.

items.en: Mackerel cured in salt then vinegar, served as sashimi or nigiri
items.note: House-cured. Curing was originally how fish survived the trip inland from Ise Bay.

items.en: Ark shell clam sliced raw — deep red, crunchy, with the frilly mantle served alongside
items.note: The mantle (himo) and the guts are usually plated with it; all three eat differently.

items.en: The adductor muscle of the pearl oyster, skewered or served raw
items.note: A true Toba speciality and a seasonal rarity: Toba is the birthplace of cultured pearls (Mikimoto Pearl Island is in the harbour), and the akoya oysters farmed for pearls yield one small sweet scallop-like muscle each. Only around when the farms harvest.

items.en: Conger eel, skewered and grilled to order, then served as nigiri — soft enough to collapse in the mouth
items.note: The chef's own boast and a long-standing local favourite; he grills each piece fresh rather than warming it. Brushed with a sweet soy glaze.

items.en: Flounder pressed between sheets of kelp for a few hours, which firms the flesh and deepens its flavour
items.note: A quiet piece of craft you rarely meet outside a proper sushi counter.

items.en: Pressed mackerel sushi — vinegared mackerel and rice moulded into a box shape and sliced, topped with a translucent sheet of kelp
items.note: A Kansai-style finisher. The name comes from Portuguese 'bateira' (boat), after its shape.

items.ja: 地酒（酒屋八兵衛・真秀 ほか）
items.en: Mie prefecture sake by the glass, alongside draft beer and soft drinks
items.note: Sakaya Hachibee (Motosaka Brewery, Odai) and Maho (Wakaebisu Brewery, Iga) are both Mie breweries. Sake is rice-based; beer is not gluten-free. Soft drinks are not priced on any menu — ask.

toba_kyubei_toba_kyubei.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed verbatim from the shop's own 料理 (menu) page at pc-nct.biz/kyube/html/ryouri.html; that domain has since lapsed, so these are the last prices the shop itself published (page content last revised c.2016, archived 2023). Drink prices are not included because the shop published its drink list as images that were never archived.

items.en: Chicken thigh, plain — the juicy dark-meat skewer, the default order
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: Two skewers to an order and every cut on this list is ¥300. The shop uses 伊勢鶏 (Ise-dori), a Mie-raised branded chicken. Grilled over charcoal; ask for shio (salt) or tare (sweet soy glaze) — tare contains wheat.

items.en: Thigh meat alternated with chunks of Japanese leek
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: The classic pairing: the leek steams inside and sweetens as it chars. 'Negi' = leek, 'ma' = in between.

items.en: Neck meat — a small, hard-working muscle, springy and unusually rich
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: Only a few dozen grams come off each bird, so it is a connoisseur's cut. Chewy-juicy rather than tender.

items.en: Chicken tail — the fatty parson's nose, elsewhere called bonjiri
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: One nub per chicken. Almost all fat and collagen; it crisps outside and bursts hot inside. 'Oppo' is this shop's homely word for what other menus print as ぼんじり.

items.en: Chicken liver — soft, mineral, almost custard-like when done right
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: 'Kimo' is the everyday word for liver; most menus print レバー. Usually glazed with tare — ask for salt if you want it lighter.

items.en: Chicken heart — small, dense, clean-tasting, with a satisfying snap
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: Written here as 'heart' in katakana; elsewhere ハツ (hatsu). Two or three hearts are threaded per skewer.

items.en: Gizzard — the muscular grinding stomach, crunchy and lean
items.section: 伊勢鶏 串焼き / Ise-Chicken Skewers
items.note: The signature crunch of a yakitori counter, with almost no fat. Best with just salt and lemon.

items.en: Deep-fried chicken wings, two to an order
items.note: Wings are a Nagoya-area obsession and Mie sits next door; expect them crisp, peppery and sticky. Floured before frying, so not gluten-free.
Pure skin fried until it shatters. A great beer snack; nothing lean about it.

items.en: Marinated boneless chicken thigh, deep-fried Japanese-style
items.note: Karaage: thigh marinated in soy, sake and ginger, dusted in flour and starch, fried twice. Squeeze the lemon before anyone else does.

items.en: Deep-fried chicken cartilage — all crunch, no meat
items.note: The knobbly cartilage from the breastbone or knee, eaten whole. The texture is the entire point.

items.en: Skewered chicken thigh in breadcrumbs, deep-fried — three skewers
items.note: Kushikatsu = crumbed and fried on a stick, dipped in a thin sweet-savoury sauce. Panko, so wheat.

items.en: Assorted sashimi of whatever came in off the boats that day
items.note: The shop's own page says the glass case is full of Toba's catch and that the day's omakase sashimi platter is the thing to order. Toba is a working port on the mouth of Ise Bay, so the line-up changes daily. Soy for dipping contains wheat.

items.ja: マグロのアボガドわさび和
items.en: Cubes of raw tuna tossed with avocado in a wasabi dressing
items.note: A modern izakaya standard — the avocado's fat stands in for tuna belly. Soy-based dressing.

items.ja: サーモンのカルパッチョ
items.en: Thin-sliced raw salmon dressed with oil, citrus and herbs
items.note: Italian in name only — a Japanese izakaya invention that is now on nearly every menu in the country.

items.en: Scallop grilled and finished with soy sauce
items.note: Butter-soft in the middle with the soy caramelising at the edges. Soy sauce means wheat.

items.en: Small local shrimp deep-fried whole — shells, heads and all
items.note: 'Utase' refers to the traditional Ise Bay sail-trawlers (utase-bune) that catch these little shrimp. Eat them entire, like a savoury crisp.

items.en: Salmon roe piled on grated daikon radish
items.note: The cold, peppery radish cuts the salt and pop of the roe. Ikura is cured in soy, so wheat is likely.

items.en: Autumn/winter only — assorted items simmered in dashi, from ¥130 a piece
items.note: You choose pieces one at a time from the simmering pot: daikon, egg, konnyaku, fish cakes. Marked 秋・冬限定 (autumn and winter only).

items.en: Cucumber batons in a lightly chilli-spiked dressing
items.note: The cheap, cold, crunchy thing you order first while you read the rest of the menu.

items.en: Chilled tofu topped with sour plum paste and tiny dried whitebait
items.note: Hiyayakko (cold tofu) dressed up: umeboshi plum for sourness, chirimen-jako whitebait for salt and crunch.

items.ja: おつまみクリームチーズ
items.en: Cream cheese served as a drinking snack
items.note: Usually cubed and often smoked or topped with something salty — a very common Japanese pairing with sake and shochu.
Vietnamese-style rolls with prawn and vegetables. Rice paper is wheat-free but the filling and dipping sauce usually are not.
Romaine, cheese, creamy dressing and croutons — the croutons and dressing are the wheat problem.

items.en: Tofu gently simmered in a kombu broth at your table
items.note: Barely-cooked tofu scooped out with a slotted spoon and dipped in ponzu or soy. Warming and very plain by design.

items.en: Amberjack collar and head bones simmered in sweet soy
items.note: 'Ara' is the frame left after filleting — cheeks, collar and belly, widely considered the best-eating parts of the fish. Messy, cheap and delicious. Simmered in soy and mirin.

items.ja: しゅうまいきのこバター焼き
items.en: Pork shumai dumplings pan-fried with mushrooms and butter
items.note: A house fixture — the shop was already selling butter-fried shumai back in 2004. Dumpling wrappers are wheat.

items.ja: アツアツカニみそグラタン
items.en: Piping-hot gratin made with crab and crab tomalley
items.note: Kani-miso is the brown, intensely savoury paste inside a crab's shell, baked here under a bubbling white sauce. Roux = wheat.
'Horumon' is izakaya shorthand for pork or beef guts — chewy, fatty and made for beer. Miso commonly contains wheat.

items.en: A house dish the shop only ever calls 'Elevator'
items.note: Listed immediately before トマベー and ジャガベー, the shop's bacon-wrapped pair, so it is probably another of that family — but the name is the owners' own joke and is nowhere explained. Worth pointing at and asking.
'Toma' from tomato, 'bē' from bacon. Grilled until the bacon crisps and the tomato collapses into it.

items.en: Potato and bacon fried in butter
items.note: The shop's older menu spelled it out: じゃが苋ベーコンバター炒め. A long-running favourite here.

items.en: Wind-dried salted shark, warmed and torn into strips
items.note: An Ise-Shima speciality found almost nowhere else in Japan: shark meat air-dried in the sea wind, historically offered at Ise Jingu and eaten at New Year. Chewy, faintly ammoniac, deeply savoury — a genuine local curiosity.

items.en: Rolled omelette made with dashi — soft, juicy, served warm
items.note: Egg beaten with dashi stock and rolled layer over layer in a rectangular pan. Contains bonito dashi and usually a splash of soy.

items.en: A bowl of rice with hot tea or dashi poured over it
items.note: The classic end-of-drinking dish: plain rice, a savoury topping, hot liquid poured over to wash the evening down.

items.en: Grilled rice ball, brushed with soy sauce and charred
items.note: The crust is the point — soy-lacquered rice toasted until it crackles. Soy sauce contains wheat.
Hand-formed salted rice, usually wrapped in nori, sometimes with a filling. Ordered to soak up the drink.

items.en: Two rice balls with a shrimp tempura tail poking out
items.note: Tenmusu were invented in Mie (Tsu city) before Nagoya adopted them — so this is a local dish on home ground. Tempura batter is wheat.

items.en: Fried wheat noodles, Japanese-style rather than sauce-heavy
items.note: 'Wafu' means seasoned with soy and dashi instead of the usual thick brown yakisoba sauce. Wheat noodles.
Saltwater eel — lighter and more delicate than the grilled freshwater unagi. Batter is wheat.
Made with dark, salty mame-miso, the Tokai region's own style — sharper and less sweet than Tokyo's pale miso soup. Bonito dashi.

toba_taishu_izakaya_mishio.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. In fact no prices were found anywhere: the shop publishes no menu online — its Tabelog 料理メニュー page is empty, Gurunavi carries none, and its Instagram and Facebook post no price lists — so every item below is a dish named by diners or by the shop's own event announcements, with no price attached. Diners describe it as inexpensive; the Tabelog spend band is ¥3,000–¥3,999. Cash only, and smoking is allowed indoors.

items.en: The adductor muscle of a pearl oyster, served raw as sashimi
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: Toba is the birthplace of the cultured pearl — Mikimoto Pearl Island is minutes away — and these oysters are farmed for pearls, not food, so the sweet, scallop-like muscle appears only briefly each year and is treated as a near-legendary local delicacy. The shop lets you have it as sashimi or dressed in sumiso (vinegared miso).

items.en: A plate of oden simmered in sweet red miso rather than clear dashi
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: One diner's plate held daikon, egg, chikuwa fish tube and hanpen. Miso oden is the Tokai region's version — Mie, Aichi and Gifu coat the pieces in dark, sweet mame-miso instead of serving them in broth.

items.en: Wind-dried salted shark, warmed and torn into strips
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: An Ise-Shima speciality found almost nowhere else: shark air-dried in the sea wind, traditionally offered at Ise Jingu and eaten at New Year. Chewy and deeply savoury — one of the most distinctive things you can order in Toba.

items.en: Sashimi of the day's local fish — what the shop is known for
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: Diners order this first and rate it highly: fatty tuna, seared sea bream, amberjack. Toba is a working fishing port, so the board changes with the boats.

items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: The marbled belly cut — richer and softer than lean red akami, and the most expensive part of the fish.

items.en: Sea bream sashimi with the skin side flash-seared
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: Blowtorching the skin makes it edible and releases the fat just beneath, so you get crisp skin over cool raw flesh.

items.en: Greater amberjack sashimi — firm, clean, slightly sweet
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: A prized member of the yellowtail family, firmer and less oily than buri.

items.en: The 'crown' — a rare cut taken from the top of a tuna's head
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: Only a small strip comes off each fish: toro-like richness with a springier bite. A regular's order, not something you find on most menus.

items.en: Locally dried fish, grilled to order
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: Split, lightly salted and dried in the sea air, then grilled. The concentrated, firmer flesh tastes far more of the fish than the fresh version does.

items.en: Grilled salmon belly — the fattiest strip of the fish
items.section: 海鮮・お造り / Seafood & Sashimi
items.note: Harasu is the trimmed belly flap: very oily, salty, and cheap because it is an offcut.

items.en: Squid pan-fried in butter and soy
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Named by diners as a family favourite here. Butter-and-soy is the classic Japanese treatment for squid and scallops.

items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Pufferfish — only handled by licensed cooks — fried on the bone. Firm, faintly sweet white meat you gnaw off the little bones.

items.en: Japanese fried chicken, marinated then floured and deep-fried
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: The default izakaya order everywhere in Japan.

items.en: A thick slice of ham in breadcrumbs, deep-fried
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Cheap, nostalgic Showa-era pub food, eaten with a squirt of Worcester-style sauce.

items.en: Tubular fish cake fried in a green, seaweed-flecked batter
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: 'Isobe' means the seashore — aonori seaweed is beaten into the batter. Chikuwa itself is steamed fish paste.

items.en: Potatoes of the 'Inca no Mezame' variety, fried or buttered
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: A Japanese potato cultivar bred from Andean stock — deep yellow and chestnut-sweet. Diners rate it among the best things here.

items.en: Chewy pan-fried potato cakes with melted cheese
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Imomochi are a Hokkaido snack: mashed potato bound with starch and griddled until crisp outside and stretchy inside.

items.en: Mountain yam, usually served raw in sticks or grated
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Crunchy and faintly slippery when raw; commonly dressed with soy, wasabi and nori.

items.en: Salted green soybeans in the pod
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Boiled in salted water; squeeze the beans straight into your mouth and leave the pods.

items.en: Fried horse mackerel marinated in sweet vinegar with onion and chilli
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: One of the two dishes the shop offers at Toba's Ama Bar street-food nights. The vinegar cuts the oil, so it eats lighter than it sounds.

items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Fatty pork belly and sour kimchi — salty, spicy, built to be eaten with beer.

items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Sweet, buttery, faintly soy-scented — a Japanese izakaya staple and the easiest order for a child.

items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: The bright red sausages of Japanese school lunchboxes, served here unironically as a drinking snack.

items.en: The small compulsory appetiser that arrives with your first drink
items.section: 揚げ物・一品 / Fried & Small Plates
items.note: Not a mistake and not free — it works as a seating charge at Japanese izakaya, usually a few hundred yen, and normally cannot be declined.

items.en: A single-portion pot of tofu simmered in kombu broth
items.note: The shop does one-person hotpots, so you can order this to yourself. Dipped in ponzu or soy.
Spicy fermented-chilli broth with pork, tofu and vegetables. Gochujang and miso both commonly contain wheat.

items.en: Fine somen noodles served hot in dashi broth
items.note: The warm winter form of chilled somen. Singled out by a diner for the quality of the broth. Somen is wheat.

items.en: Ise udon, fried rather than served in soup
items.note: Ise udon is the local noodle: unusually thick and deliberately soft, dressed in a small pool of very dark, sweet tamari sauce rather than swimming in broth. Pilgrims to Ise Jingu have eaten it for centuries. Wheat noodles.

items.en: Fat rolled sushi cut into thick rounds
items.note: A thick nori roll with several fillings — egg, gourd, cucumber, fish — ordered here as the closing rice dish.

items.en: Local Mie sake — three labels kept, including Gizaemon and Hanzo
items.note: Both are Mie breweries: Gizaemon from Iga and Hanzo (named after the ninja Hattori Hanzo) from Nabari. Ask for a chilled glass and let the staff choose.

items.en: Shochu and soda with lemon — the standard cheap long drink
items.note: Light, sour and about as low-commitment as Japanese drinking gets. Listed by the shop among its Ama Bar event drinks.

items.en: Sweet-potato shochu topped up with soda
items.note: Imo-jochu is distilled from sweet potato and carries a distinct earthy sweetness. Distilled from potato rather than barley, but ask what it is cut with.

toba_senmonten.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from a photograph of the shop's own numbered laminated menu card posted in January 2026, cross-checked against a photograph of the same card from March 2024 on which every price was roughly ¥100 lower. Hours printed on the card: PM6:00–9:00, closed Mondays. The menu numbering skips several numbers — that is how the card is printed.

items.ja: 特選ロース（厚切、サイコロ）
items.en: Top-grade loin, cut thick or in dice — the best beef in the house
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: 'Rosu' is loin/sirloin: leaner than karubi, tender, strongly beefy. Atsugiri = thick-cut, saikoro = 'dice', cubed steak-style. You grill it yourself over the tabletop fire. Mie is Matsusaka beef country and reviewers come here for the marbling.

items.en: Beef loin — the standard tender, leaner cut
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: The safe first order at any yakiniku: sear both sides briefly and pull it while still pink. Dipping tare is soy-based; ask for salt if you must avoid wheat.

items.en: Short rib — the fatty, sweet, sizzling cut yakiniku is built around
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: From the belly and rib. It flares on the grill because of the fat, so keep it moving. Karubi and rosu are the two poles of any yakiniku menu: fatty versus lean.

items.en: Beef tongue with salt — thin slices, seconds a side
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: Tongue is springy rather than tender and is traditionally eaten first, with salt and lemon, before sweet sauce muddies your palate. Salt-seasoned rather than soy, but confirm.

items.en: Premium tripe — the cow's first stomach, thick and crunchy
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: The menu glosses it 'cow's stomach'. Mino is scored in a criss-cross so it curls on the grill; firm and squeaky, with almost no flavour of its own. 'Jo' marks the upper grade.

items.en: Beef tongue marinated in sweet soy tare
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: The same tongue as shio-tan but pre-soaked in the house sweet-soy marinade. Tare is soy- and therefore wheat-based.

items.en: Large intestine — the fat-lined, chewy king of horumon
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: Grill it fat-side down until it puffs and blisters; it goes from rubbery to melting if you are patient. Sold elsewhere as shimacho.

items.en: Heart — dense, lean and clean-tasting; nothing like liver
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: The name is from English 'heart'. Best cooked barely through, with salt.

items.en: Beef liver — soft, iron-rich, sweet when just cooked through
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: Japanese law bans serving beef liver raw, so it comes to be grilled. A reviewer here singled it out as unusually fresh. Often eaten with sesame oil and salt.

items.en: Small intestine — fatty, chewy tubes; the classic offal order
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: 'Horumon' is the general Japanese word for grilled offal, from the Osaka joke that it is 'the stuff you throw away' (horu mon). Cheap and enormously popular.

items.en: Young chicken, cut for the grill
items.section: 焼肉・内臓 / Grilled Meat & Offal
items.note: The one non-beef item on the grill list. Unlike the beef, cook it right through.

items.en: Mixed seafood platter for the grill — prawn, scallop and squid
items.note: Toba is a fishing port, so even the yakiniku shop grills seafood. The platter is cheaper than the three ordered separately.
Grilled in the shell; the heads are the best part if you are brave.
Take them off the moment the edges firm — overcooked scallop turns to rubber.
Sweet and springy; a quick sear each side is enough.

items.ja: 牛肉刺身（生姜醤油のたれで）
items.en: Raw beef sashimi, eaten with a ginger-soy dip
items.note: Sliced raw beef with the shop's ginger-and-soy sauce, exactly as the menu specifies. Soy sauce means wheat.

items.en: Korean-style raw beef, hand-cut into strips and seasoned
items.note: The menu explains it: lean beef shredded fine and dressed — usually sesame oil, soy and a raw egg yolk. Rare in Japan since the 2011 food-safety crackdown, so finding it on a menu at all is notable.

items.ja: 生タン（生姜醤油のたれで）
items.en: Raw beef tongue, served with a ginger-soy dip
items.note: Thin raw slices — cool, faintly sweet, far softer than the grilled version.

items.ja: 生センマイ（酢味噌のたれで）
items.en: Raw omasum — the frilly 'thousand-leaf' third stomach
items.note: Served with sumiso (vinegared miso), as the menu states. Black-and-white ruffled sheets with a cool, crisp bite and little taste of their own — a texture dish. Miso contains wheat.

items.section: 野菜・サラダ / Vegetables & Salad
items.note: Usually onion, pumpkin, peppers and mushrooms — and they cook on the same grill as the meat.

items.en: Leaf lettuce for wrapping your grilled meat
items.section: 野菜・サラダ / Vegetables & Salad
items.note: 'Chisha' is the old Japanese word for lettuce; this is the Korean ssam leaf. Put a hot slice of meat in it with rice and a dab of miso and eat it in one bite.

items.en: Korean seasoned vegetables — a mixed plate
items.section: 野菜・サラダ / Vegetables & Salad
items.note: The menu names the possible components: namasu, bean sprouts, bracken fern (zenmai), garlic chives or spinach, each blanched and dressed with sesame oil, garlic and salt.

items.section: 野菜・サラダ / Vegetables & Salad
items.note: Cheap, cold and crunchy, there to cut the fat between mouthfuls of grilled beef. Usually comes with a sesame or miso dip.

items.section: 野菜・サラダ / Vegetables & Salad
items.note: Whatever the shop has in that month — worth asking what is in it.

items.section: 野菜・サラダ / Vegetables & Salad
items.note: Fine white threads of raw radish, usually with nori and a soy or sesame dressing. Peppery and very refreshing at a grill table.
The menu specifies the Chinese-cabbage kind. Kimchi often contains fish sauce or salted shrimp, so it is not reliably vegan.
Kkakdugi in Korean — chunkier, juicier and crunchier than the cabbage version.

items.ja: 漬物盛り合わせ（キムチ、カクテキ）
items.en: Pickle plate — both kimchi and kakuteki
items.note: Cheaper than ordering the two separately.

items.en: Spicy Korean beef and vegetable soup
items.note: Shredded beef, bean sprouts and chilli in a red, fiery broth. Gochujang and soy both usually contain wheat.
A clear, restorative broth heavy with garlic — an end-of-evening order.
Light broth, but at a yakiniku shop the stock is usually beef-based — ask.
Clean and slightly sweet, with a sesame finish.
Silky wakame in a light sesame-scented broth — the Korean miyeokguk idea, lightened.
Beaten egg swirled into hot broth into ribbons.
Dark, salty mame-miso soup — the Tokai region's own style, sharper than Tokyo's pale miso. Made with bonito dashi.
Order it early — grilled meat without rice gets heavy fast.
The small bowl. At a yakiniku restaurant the rice is the point of the meal, not a side — you grill a piece of meat, dip it in tare and eat it over the rice.

items.en: Bibimbap served in a scorching stone bowl
items.note: The stone bowl keeps cooking the rice at the table, so a crisp brown crust forms on the bottom — stir everything hard the moment it lands. Chilli paste usually contains wheat.

items.en: The spicy beef soup poured over a bowl of rice
items.note: The menu spells it out: a spicy beef-and-vegetable soup ladled over rice, served as a meal.

items.en: Mixed rice bowl with seasoned vegetables
items.note: The menu describes it as assorted vegetables and aromatics arranged over rice, to be mixed — the plain-bowl version, without the hot stone.
Gukbap: rice served in a beef broth. The gentlest thing on the menu and a good way to end.

items.ja: 焼肉弁当（お持ち帰りのみ）
items.note: Marked お持ち帰りのみ: you cannot eat it in. Tare-glazed beef over rice.
A handwritten notice photographed in the shop in January 2026 read ただいま生ビール販売停止中です — draught temporarily suspended — so check before ordering. Beer is barley.

items.ja: びんビール（キリン、中瓶）
items.note: The fallback when the draught line is down.
One 'go' is the standard Japanese measure, roughly a small carafe.

items.en: Shochu highball — lemon and other flavours
items.note: Shochu with soda and a flavouring. Light and sour, and it cuts through grilled fat well.

items.en: Shochu cut with plum — sweet-sour and easy
items.note: Umeshu plum liqueur or plum syrup mixed into shochu.

items.en: Oolong tea — the standard non-alcoholic order
items.note: Served cold and unsweetened; the default drink for whoever is driving.
The cold, sharp full stop after an hour of grilled beef.
Melon is a luxury fruit in Japan and its flavour turns up everywhere as a treat.
Yuzu is a fragrant Japanese citrus, more perfume than juice — the most local-tasting of the three.

toba_sasazuki.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the shop's own printed menu sheet and daily whiteboard, photographed July 2023.

items.en: Ramen in a light vegetable-based broth with four pieces of hot, just-fried chicken karaage dropped straight into the bowl
items.note: The shop's signature and the reason people drive here. The owner puts the fried chicken into the soup on purpose so it softens and is easier to eat, and she switched the broth to a vegetable base because she worries about her customers' health. Comes with a boiled egg and a slice of pink-and-white kamaboko fish cake.

items.en: The karaage ramen served as a full set with rice, and small side dishes
items.note: The biggest meal on the board. The kobachi (little side bowls) change daily — regulars have reported tuna sashimi, simmered daikon with fried tofu, soy-simmered egg and mozuku seaweed.

items.en: A bowl of old-fashioned soy-sauce ramen plus a bowl of rice and daily side dishes
items.note: The most-ordered set. The ramen is chicken-based, light but with real depth, thin-to-medium straight noodles, two thick slices of pork belly chashu, naruto fish cake and a boiled egg. The rice arrives with noritama furikake sprinkled on top. Yes, Japanese people really do eat rice with their ramen.

items.en: Ramen piled with stir-fried vegetables, served as a set with rice and side dishes
items.note: The vegetable version of the set — cabbage, bean sprouts, onion and carrot stir-fried and heaped on the noodles. The broth itself is not vegetarian.

items.ja: ラーメンとチキンのみそかつ丼
items.en: A bowl of ramen paired with a small rice bowl of crumbed fried chicken under Nagoya-style sweet red-miso sauce
items.note: Misokatsu is a Chubu-region speciality: a fried cutlet glossed with thick, sweet-savoury red miso sauce rather than the usual brown tonkatsu sauce. Here it is chicken, over rice, with the ramen alongside.

items.en: Thin slices of pork pan-fried with grated ginger, soy and mirin, with rice, soup and sides
items.note: The default Japanese lunchtime set meal — sweet, salty, gingery pork with shredded raw cabbage. Reliably good and nothing strange in it.

items.en: Japanese fried chicken — marinated in soy, sake and ginger, dusted in potato starch and fried — with rice, soup and sides
items.note: The same karaage that goes into the signature ramen, served as a plate of its own.

items.en: Chef's-choice set — whatever the owner has cooked and bought that day
items.note: The gamble worth taking: one diner reported it arriving as sashimi plus sukiyaki-style simmered beef. Point at the words 'おまかせ定食' and let the owner decide.

items.en: A plate of Japanese-style fried chicken, no rice
items.note: Ordered as a dish to share or to drink with. A larger portion, 唐揚げ大, is ¥1,200.

items.en: Large plate of Japanese-style fried chicken
items.note: The sharing size. 大 (dai) simply means 'large'.

items.en: Stir-fried mixed vegetables — cabbage, bean sprouts, onion, carrot, usually with a little pork
items.note: Ask for it without pork if you need to — 'butaniku nashi de' — but the seasoning is soy-based either way.

items.en: Ginger pork on its own, without the rice-and-soup set
items.note: Also chalked on the daily whiteboard at the same price.

items.en: Root vegetables, konnyaku and often chicken slow-simmered in dashi and soy until dark and sweet
items.note: Proper Japanese home cooking — the kind of dish you only get at a shop run by one person who has cooked it for forty years. Served warm or at room temperature.

items.en: A block of chilled silken tofu with spring onion, ginger and soy sauce poured over
items.note: Short for hiya-yakko. The cheapest thing on the menu and a good cooling counterpoint to fried chicken. Usually topped with bonito flakes unless you ask otherwise.

items.en: A breaded pork cutlet simmered with onion in sweet dashi-soy broth and bound with beaten egg
items.section: 本日のおすすめ（黒板） / Daily specials board
items.note: Essentially the topping of a katsu-don served in its own bowl rather than over rice. Soft, sweet and eggy.

items.en: Minced fatty tuna belly mixed with chopped spring onion, eaten raw
items.section: 本日のおすすめ（黒板） / Daily specials board
items.note: Toba is a working fishing port, so raw fish turns up even at a noodle-and-set-meal shokudo. Eat with a little soy sauce.

items.en: Sliced fresh tomato salad, usually with onion and a light dressing
items.section: 本日のおすすめ（黒板） / Daily specials board
items.note: From the handwritten whiteboard of the day's extras. The dressing is likely soy- or mayo-based, so check if it matters.
The shop is open 11:00-19:00, so this is a lunchtime-and-early-evening beer rather than a night out.

items.en: Shochu — Japanese distilled spirit, usually from barley or sweet potato, drunk with hot water or ice
items.note: Ask which base they pour; barley (mugi) is lighter, sweet potato (imo) is earthier.

items.en: Sake — brewed rice wine, served by the glass
items.note: On this menu お酒 means nihonshu (sake) specifically, not 'alcohol' in general.

toba_benkei.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from photographs of the shop's own in-store printed menu card (latest posted version). The menu states すべて税込み価格です — all prices tax-included.

items.en: Plain old-school soy-sauce ramen — clear brown broth, thin straight noodles, chashu pork, menma and spring onion
items.note: This is chuka-soba, the pre-boom Showa-era style of ramen you find in a machi-chuka (neighbourhood Chinese diner) rather than a specialist ramen shop. Gentle, not heavy.

items.en: Ramen in a broth thickened and seasoned with fermented soybean paste
items.note: Richer, sweeter and cloudier than the soy version. Miso is made with barley or rice koji and is not wheat-free here.

items.en: Ramen topped with a stir-fry of pork, squid or prawn, cabbage, carrot, wood-ear mushroom and quail egg
items.note: 五目 literally means 'five things' but really means 'lots of assorted ingredients'. A good all-rounder if you want vegetables with your noodles.

items.en: Noodles in a milky-white broth cooked together with pork, seafood and vegetables
items.note: Champon began in Nagasaki as a cheap, filling dish for Chinese students; everything is stir-fried in the pot then the soup and noodles go in on top, so the broth carries all the flavours.

items.en: The plain soy ramen with a much bigger pile of braised sliced pork belly
items.note: Reviewers report three generous slices. The miso version, みそチャーシューメン, is ¥800.

items.en: Wheat noodles stir-fried with pork and cabbage in a tangy-sweet brown sauce
items.note: Chinese-restaurant yakisoba is usually saltier and less sauce-heavy than the festival-stall kind.

items.en: Pan-fried noodles under a thick, glossy starch-bound sauce of pork, seafood and vegetables
items.note: 'Ankake' means the sauce is thickened with potato starch so it clings to the noodles and stays hot for a long time. Careful on the first bite.

items.en: Deep-fried crisp noodles smothered in the same thick seafood-and-vegetable ankake sauce, so they soften as you eat
items.note: A regional name — a diner here described it as 'bari-soba', the crunchy-noodle style. Half the pleasure is the contrast between the shattering crisp bits and the parts that have gone soft under the sauce.

items.en: Chilled summer noodles with strips of ham, cucumber, egg and tomato, dressed in cold vinegar-soy sauce
items.note: Summer only — also advertised on the wall as 冷し中華 (hiyashi-chuka). Sour, cold and refreshing rather than soupy.

items.en: Fried rice with egg, spring onion and roast pork
items.note: Comes out in about three minutes. A half portion, チャーハン（ハーフ）, is ¥360 if you want it alongside noodles.

items.en: Stir-fried pork, seafood and vegetables in a thickened sauce poured over a bowl of rice
items.note: Also written 中華丼. The classic one-bowl machi-chuka lunch — basically happosai (see below) served on rice. Two more rice bowls sit beside it: ホイコーロー飯 (twice-cooked pork with cabbage in sweet bean sauce) and チンジャオニューロー飯 (shredded beef with green pepper and bamboo shoot), both ¥780. ぞうすい, a soft savoury rice porridge, is ¥600.

items.en: A crab-and-egg omelette laid over rice and covered in a glossy sweet-and-sour thickened sauce
items.note: Soft, mild and slightly sweet — one of the most comforting things on any Japanese Chinese menu. The same topping over ramen noodles instead of rice is 天津メン (tenshin-men), ¥630.

items.en: Mapo tofu — soft tofu and minced pork in a spicy fermented-bean sauce — spooned over rice
items.note: Japanese mapo is much milder than the Sichuan original, with little or none of the numbing sansho pepper.

items.en: The house combination plate: sweet-and-sour pork, fried chicken and stir-fried vegetables in thick sauce on one dish, with rice, soup and pickles
items.note: Named after the shop itself and the biggest thing on the menu — if you want to try three of their signatures in one go, this is it.

items.en: Sweet-and-sour pork set — battered pork chunks with pepper, onion and pineapple-free vinegar sauce, plus rice and soup
items.note: One of the three dishes reviewers name most often here (with gyoza and karaage). Sold on its own as 酢豚 for ¥930.

items.en: Stir-fried cabbage, bean sprouts, carrot and pork with rice and soup
items.note: The cheapest set. Its sibling もやし炒め定食 (bean sprout) is the same ¥940; ニラ炒め定食 (garlic chives) is ¥1,020.

items.en: Japanese fried chicken set — soy-and-ginger marinated chicken, fried crisp, with rice and soup
items.note: A house favourite. À la carte からあげ is ¥910.

items.en: Aubergine stir-fried with minced pork in a sweet-savoury miso sauce, with rice and soup
items.note: The aubergine is fried first so it goes silky and soaks up the miso. One of the shop's best-photographed dishes.

items.en: 'Eight treasures' — pork, prawn, squid, quail egg and assorted vegetables in a thick clear sauce, with rice and soup
items.note: The same thing that goes on top of chuka-han, served as a proper set. Mild and not at all spicy.

items.en: Pan-fried pork-and-cabbage dumplings, crisp on the bottom
items.section: 一品料理 / À la carte
items.note: Dip in the soy-vinegar-chilli oil mixed at your table. The most-mentioned dish in reviews of this shop.

items.en: Soft tofu and minced pork in a mildly spicy fermented-bean sauce, thickened with starch
items.section: 一品料理 / À la carte
items.note: Order rice separately (ライス 小 ¥210 / 中 ¥260 / 大 ¥270) or take the 麻婆飯 rice-bowl version. カニ玉子焼き / エビ玉子焼き — crab or prawn folded into a fluffy egg cake under thickened sauce — are ¥910 each.

items.en: Prawns in a sweet, mildly hot tomato-and-chilli sauce
items.section: 一品料理 / À la carte
items.note: The priciest single dish here. Japanese ebi-chili is sweeter and far less fiery than its Sichuan ancestor.

items.en: Fried chicken wings glazed in sweet-salty sauce and dusted with pepper and sesame
items.section: 一品料理 / À la carte
items.note: A Nagoya/Chubu bar staple that has spread across the region. Eaten with your hands, best with the beer.
Bottled beer (ビール 中瓶) is also ¥550; a non-alcoholic beer is ¥400. Four shochu and a plum liqueur (青谷の梅) are ¥500 each; 玉子スープ, an egg-ribbon broth, is ¥440.

items.en: Shaoxing wine — dark, aged Chinese rice wine, served warm
items.note: Made with wheat-based starter, so not gluten-free. Traditionally drunk warm, sometimes with a little rock sugar.

toba_cuccagna_toba.price_note: Taken from the restaurant's own website menu pages. A ¥500 per-person cover charge applies from 18:00. At lunch (11:00-14:30 LO) the kitchen runs a pasta-only menu of about ten dishes with salad and bread from around ¥1,100, plus ¥200 for dessert and a drink. Prices approximate — may change.

items.ja: 伊勢エビのペスカトーラ トマトクリームソースパスタ or クリームソースパスタ
items.en: Pasta with a whole local spiny lobster, in either tomato-cream or plain cream sauce
items.note: Ise-ebi is the spiny lobster of Ise-Shima — sweeter and firmer than a northern lobster, and the single most prized thing caught off this coast. Season peaks roughly October to April. The most expensive and most local dish on the menu; you choose the sauce when you order.

items.en: Seafood pasta — prawns, squid, clams and whatever the boats brought in, in tomato sauce
items.note: The house standard and what most regulars order. Toba is a working fishing port, so the shellfish are genuinely local.

items.ja: 牡蠣とベーコンのトマトソース
items.romaji: Kaki to bacon no tomato sauce
items.en: Pasta with oysters and bacon in tomato sauce
items.note: Toba and neighbouring Ura-mura are one of Japan's great oyster-farming bays; winter is the season. Smoky bacon against briny oyster is the point of the dish.

items.ja: 牡蠣とアオサのクリーム生パスタ
items.romaji: Kaki to aosa no cream nama-pasta
items.en: Fresh pasta with oysters and aosa seaweed in cream sauce
items.note: Aosa is a bright green sea lettuce harvested in the shallow bays of Ise-Shima and dried; it smells intensely of the sea and turns the cream green. About as Toba as Italian food gets. 生パスタ means fresh, not dried, pasta.

items.ja: 魚介ときのこのオイルパスタ
items.romaji: Gyokai to kinoko no oil pasta
items.en: Seafood and mushroom pasta dressed simply in garlic and olive oil, no sauce
items.note: The lightest of the seafood pastas — good if you want to taste the fish rather than tomato or cream.

items.en: Spaghetti with garlic, chilli and olive oil only
items.note: The cheapest plate on the menu and the safest bet for anyone avoiding dairy and seafood — but confirm there is no anchovy or bacon in it.

items.ja: ペンネ アラビアータ
items.note: Also on the menu: ペンネ ゴルゴンゾーラ, penne in blue-cheese cream, ¥1,500.

items.ja: カボチャとベーコンのクリーム ニョッキ
items.romaji: Kabocha to bacon no cream gnocchi
items.en: Potato gnocchi with Japanese pumpkin and bacon in cream sauce
items.note: Gnocchi are soft little potato dumplings rather than noodles; kabocha pumpkin is denser and sweeter than a Western one.

items.ja: カポナータとバケット（あおさパン）
items.en: Sicilian sweet-and-sour stewed aubergine with bread made with local aosa seaweed
items.note: The bread is the local touch — green-flecked and faintly marine. Caponata itself is aubergine, celery, olives and capers cooked down with vinegar and sugar; usually vegan but confirm.

items.en: Mixed antipasto plate — the kitchen's selection of small starters
items.note: The easiest way to see what the chef is doing with local produce that week without reading the menu.

items.ja: 地場野菜のバーニャカウダ
items.en: Local raw vegetables served with a warm dip of garlic, anchovy and olive oil
items.note: 地場野菜 means the vegetables were grown nearby in Mie. The dip contains anchovy, so it is not vegetarian.

items.ja: 魚介のマリネのサラダ
items.en: Salad of local seafood marinated in olive oil, lemon and herbs
items.note: A good cold introduction to what is swimming off Toba — usually white fish, squid and shellfish, lightly cured rather than cooked.

items.en: Sliced tomato and mozzarella with basil and olive oil
items.note: Naturally gluten-free as long as no bread comes with it.

items.en: Chicken gizzards slow-cooked in their own fat until tender
items.note: Springy rather than chewy when done properly. A cheap, very good thing to drink with.

items.en: Herb-roasted Ise chicken — a Mie-branded free-range breed
items.note: Ise-dori is raised locally and has firmer, more flavourful meat than commodity chicken. Roasted with rosemary and other herbs.

items.en: Seared Ise beef sliced thin and served rare over rocket with olive oil
items.note: Ise-gyu is Mie's own wagyu, from the same prefecture and tradition as Matsusaka beef. Tagliata means 'cut' — a whole seared steak sliced across the grain and eaten as a sharing plate.

items.ja: カマンベールのオーブン焼き
items.en: A whole Camembert baked until molten, for scooping with bread
